chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from 'Ubayd Allah and 'Imran, the two sons of 'Ali al-Halabiyy, who said:

We used to dispute on the road concerning the prayer, the night prayer ('Isha'), before the disappearance of the twilight, and among us were those whose hearts felt uneasy about that. So we entered upon Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام and asked him about performing the night prayer before the disappearance of the twilight. He said: There is no harm in that. We said: And what is the twilight? He said: The redness.

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight referred to in legal discussion of prayer time
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the redness in the sky, defined here as al-shafaq
key_terms.سُقُوطِ الشَّفَقِ: the disappearance of twilight, marking a time-related boundary under discussion
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ: the night prayer ('Isha), the final evening salat
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of permissibility
key_terms.نَخْتَصِمُ: we disputed or differed, indicating disagreement over the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat al-'isha' before the twilight disappears?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the time of salat al-'isha' and reports that Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permitted performing it before the disappearance of the twilight. He then identified al-shafaq as the redness, clarifying an important juristic term related to prayer timing.
